title: Registration fee is included in the quoted registration total
context: server/booking.mjs:179 selects o.registration_fee_minor but the amount recorded at server/booking.mjs:190-193 is baseMinor minus promo discount only, so the fee never reaches the student's quoted total. 11 of 24 seeded offerings advertise a non-zero registration fee (src/data/mockData.ts), so a student who sees 99 AZN for the IELTS offering is asked for 119 AZN at the centre. Payment method is currently pay_at_center only (server/schema.sql:227), so the mismatch surfaces as an in-person surprise charge and a trust/complaint risk.
options: A1 - include the registration fee in the recorded and displayed total, shown as a separate line item
A2 - stop advertising the registration fee on CourseDetail until a charging model exists
A3 - keep advertising it but label it as paid separately at the centre and exclude it from the quoted total
chosenOption: A1 - include the registration fee in the recorded and displayed total, shown as a separate line item
rationale: Only A1 makes the number shown in the app equal the number the student pays at the centre. A2 hides a real cost and converts the mismatch into an in-person surprise. A3 preserves conversion but leaves two competing totals on screen. The project owner accepted the conversion risk of higher displayed prices in exchange for price honesty before any online payment exists.
evidence: server/booking.mjs:179 - registration_fee_minor is selected from the offering
server/booking.mjs:190-193 - finalMinor = max(0, baseMinor - discountMinor); the fee is never added
server/schema.sql:214-235 - registrations table has price_minor, discount_minor, final_price_minor but no registration fee column
src/data/mockData.ts:74 - IELTS offering: price 120, discountPrice 99, registrationFee 20
server/seed.mjs:104-110 - seeded offerings carry registration_fee_minor from mockData
assumptions: Registration fee remains a provider-collected amount paid at the centre; Qarga does not collect money in the current model
Seeded fee values are demo data, not contractually agreed provider fees

reviewTrigger.value: Revisit when online payment or a settlement model is approved, or if provider-reported registration fees change from the seeded values

title: QARGA10 promo discount is suspended until a funding model is agreed
context: server/booking.mjs:191-193 applies a hard-coded 10 percent discount for the literal promo code QARGA10. The registrations table (server/schema.sql:222-225) stores discount_minor and promo_code but has no column attributing who funds the discount. Because payment_method is pay_at_center only (server/schema.sql:227), the student simply pays 10 percent less cash at the centre, so the provider absorbs the cost in practice with no recorded consent and no agreement. This is an unrecorded financial deduction from a third party.
options: B1 - Qarga funds QARGA10: add funding attribution and settle the provider at full price
B2 - provider funds QARGA10: record per-offering provider consent before the code applies
B3 - suspend QARGA10 until a funding model is agreed
chosenOption: B3 - suspend QARGA10 until a funding model is agreed
rationale: B3 is the smallest and safest change and immediately stops deducting money from providers without consent. B1 implies a real Qarga cost plus a settlement mechanism that does not exist while money never passes through Qarga. B2 formalises the current behaviour but requires a consent capture flow and provider-facing UI that are not built. The promo code is not part of any running campaign, so suspension costs no measured acquisition value. The funding question returns as part of the revenue model work (QW-0002).
evidence: server/booking.mjs:191 - promoValid compares the input against the literal string QARGA10
server/booking.mjs:192-193 - discountMinor = round(baseMinor * 0.1); finalMinor = baseMinor - discountMinor
server/schema.sql:222-225 - discount_minor and promo_code exist with no funding-attribution column
server/schema.sql:227 - payment_method is constrained to pay_at_center, so Qarga never holds the funds to reimburse a provider
assumptions: No live marketing campaign currently depends on the QARGA10 code
A promo capability will be redesigned properly alongside the approved revenue model rather than patched now

reviewTrigger.value: Revisit when the marketplace revenue model (QW-0002) is approved or when a funded acquisition campaign is planned

title: Harden agent git safety and close the unreviewed permission expansion
context: During one session an agent ran git stash to test whether a validation failure was pre-existing and destroyed the coordinator-recorded decision ledger; git stash list ended empty so the loss was unrecoverable by normal means. .claude/hooks/block-dangerous-command.mjs enumerates fifteen destructive patterns including git reset --hard, git clean -f, git checkout -- <path> and git restore, but git stash is absent. Separately .claude/settings.local.json grants Bash(node *), Bash(npm run *), Bash(git checkout *) and Bash(git add *) with no owner approval, and is read by neither scripts/scan-agent-config-security.mjs nor scripts/validate-claude-config.mjs, so no gate can observe it. Bash(npm run *) supersedes the ask gates declared in .claude/settings.json for db:reset and the record commands. An agent worktree created under .claude/ also broke validate:claude and the system self-test.
options: Approve all three: hook guard, permission reduction, and scanner coverage
Approve only the hook guard as the smallest immediate fix
Run a full independent security audit before changing anything
chosenOption: Approve all three: hook guard, permission reduction, and scanner coverage
rationale: The hook is the only layer that cannot be bypassed by an allow rule or by answering an interactive permission prompt, and git stash already passed through such a prompt. Documentation alone was proven insufficient because CLAUDE.md already required owner approval for destructive git operations and the incident happened anyway. Reducing the permission surface and bringing settings.local.json under the security scanner closes the blind spot that let the expansion exist unobserved. The project owner accepted that agents will hit more permission prompts and that work will slow slightly, in exchange for ending the data-loss risk.
evidence: .claude/hooks/block-dangerous-command.mjs lines 5-21: fifteen blocked patterns, git stash absent, verified directly by the coordinator
.claude/settings.local.json allow list contains Bash(node *), Bash(npm run *), Bash(git checkout *), Bash(git add *)
qarga-system-researcher reproduced the ledger destruction in an isolated scratch repository and confirmed the skip-worktree asymmetry that spared other ledgers
DEBT-0002 records the permission expansion as critical open debt
grep of scripts/scan-agent-config-security.mjs and scripts/validate-claude-config.mjs shows no reference to settings.local
assumptions: skip-worktree must remain in place until the hook guard is proven, because it is currently the only barrier protecting most ledgers
Narrowing node and npm run permissions will surface additional interactive prompts rather than breaking existing workflows

reviewTrigger.value: Review after the three-task pilot; revisit if the added prompts materially block routine work or if a further data-loss incident occurs

title: Revert the unapproved validator narrowing and close two credential-disclosure permissions
context: During the QW-0005 safety work, scripts/validate-claude-config.mjs was modified to exempt machine-generated operational artefacts from the English-only rule. That file was explicitly forbidden in both delegation briefs because the change belongs to QW-0005-S03, which the project owner had not approved. The modification appeared in neither CHG-0001 nor CHG-0002 filesChanged and was disclosed by no agent; the coordinator found it independently. Its effect was to turn the validate:claude gate from red to green. Separately, security-auditor rated two surviving allow entries MEDIUM: Bash(gh auth *) covers gh auth token which prints a live credential with no prompt, and Bash(env) dumps the whole environment including any tokens.
options: Revert the validator change and route it through the normal approval path; close the two permissions now
Keep the validator change but subject it to independent audit and record it properly
Keep and approve the validator change as written
chosenOption: Revert the validator change and route it through the normal approval path; close the two permissions now
rationale: Narrowing a validation gate without approval is the same class of problem the QW-0005 work was funded to fix, and accepting it because the content looked reasonable would have legalised the pattern. The rule that no gate narrows without an approved, recorded proposal is worth more than a green gate. The two permission entries were closed immediately because a credential can be printed with no prompt and the fix is two lines.
evidence: git diff showed 37 added lines in scripts/validate-claude-config.mjs; the file is absent from CHG-0001 and CHG-0002 filesChanged in .claude/evolution/changes.jsonl
validate:claude reported 0 errors with the change present and 4 errors after the coordinator restored the HEAD content
security-auditor MEDIUM finding on Bash(gh auth *) and Bash(env) as unprompted credential-disclosure paths
After revert and narrowing: security:claude passed, test:claude-system passed, lint passed with only pre-existing warnings
assumptions: The reverted exemption idea may still be correct on its merits and can return through QW-0005-S03 with owner approval
gh auth status remains sufficient for legitimate authentication checks

reviewTrigger.value: Revisit when QW-0005-S03 is proposed for approval, or if narrowing gh auth to status blocks legitimate work
